nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What is the main focus of SSI education?
nodes.answer: SSI education focuses on developing students' ethical reasoning and character, promoting decision-making based on moral judgments through public discourse and argumentation.
nodes.paragraph: Moreover, SSI education focuses on developing students ethical reasoning and character, promoting decision-making based on moral judgments through engagement in public discourse and argumentation (Zei- dler, 2014). Research in Science Education Various factors bring challenges to SSI teaching for teachers. The lack of pedagogical content knowledge and instructional confidence is one of the barriers influencing teachers willingness to teach SSI (Kinskey & Zeidler, 2024). Due to lower confidence in discuss- ing controversial issues, teachers usually feel unprepared to balance subject content and ethical discussions, especially in areas with sociocultural and religious conflicts (Relela & Mavuru, 2023). Moreover, teachers often adopt a neutral or value-free stance in the classroom to avoid controversy and perceptions of indoctrination, stemming from concerns about maintaining neutrality (Ozcan-Ermis & Herv , 2024). Additionally, practical chal- lenges like limited curriculum time, scarce resources specific to SSI instruction, and diffi- culties in assessing student learning in these areas further complicate SSI teaching (Nielsen et al., 2020). To overcome teachers pedagogical challenges, several studies have investigated how to effectively improve teachers professional development (PD) for SSI teaching (Bayram- Jacobs et al., 2019; Friedrichsen et al., 2020; Kinskey & Zeidler, 2024; Leung, 2022).

nodes.question: Why is it important for young people to acquire civic knowledge, according to the paragraph?
nodes.answer: It is important for young people to acquire civic knowledge to develop their abilities to contribute to broader societal issues, such as understanding citizenship, political institutions, human rights, environmental concerns, and global issues.
nodes.paragraph: Compared to adults, adolescents have been found to have more positive attitudes toward using robots, for example inpsychotherapy [ 45]. This may be due to teenagers being gen- erally more ready to adopt new technologies [ 46]. However, in the workplace context, Fenech et al. [ 47] found that gen- eration Z (i.e., people born between 1997 and 2012) has anundecided attitude toward robotics, which may lean toward apprehension, fear, and anxiety. In some previous studies, young people have been engaged through a participatorydesign approach to ideate social robots for mental health. Bj rling and Rose [ 29] conducted an extensive social robot design challenge with young people in a school environment,drawing from previous research suggesting that robots canhave therapeutic effects on humans emotional responses. The aim of the challenge was to design a social robot to help reduce stress, and the study resulted in various ideasfor robot embodiments and features [ 48]. The participants engaged in design sessions that included activities ranging from drawing to storyboarding and testing a robot prototypewith peers.
